_meta.purpose: Track per-skill quality scores across invocations

scoring_rubric.10: Flawless — perfect execution, exceeded expectations, zero rework
scoring_rubric.9: Excellent — all success criteria met, minimal polish
scoring_rubric.8: Strong — correct execution, minor adjustments only
scoring_rubric.7: Good — correct, one small correction needed

runs.arguments:
Deliverable: a focused Tech Radar / Architecture Review answering "what tech stack fits THIS codebase" — validate current choices and recommend complementary stack to productionize it. Ground it in the actual current state below; do NOT propose a from-scratch rewrite. Output as a chat response (and optionally a NEW file docs/TECH_STACK.md) — do NOT modify README.md or any wiki file (a docs workflow is currently editing those).

== THE CODEBASE (verified this session) ==
- mdm-api: a STANDALONE, single-domain Go API (KPM = Kelompok Penerima Manfaat, BGN MBG program). Just migrated from Rust/Axum to Go. Not a microservice — single self-contained binary (cmd/api) behind the Kong API gateway. Only outbound deps: PostgreSQL/PostGIS (read-only "gold" OLAP schema + optional read replica) and an optional OTLP collector. Read-mostly: write endpoints return 400 by design.
- Module: go 1.25 (built with go 1.26.3 via asdf). Standard Go layout (cmd/api + internal/{config,domain,dto,apperror,middleware,repository/postgres,handler,router,telemetry,state}). 131 tests pass, go build/vet/gofmt green.

== CURRENT STACK (already chosen, in use) ==
- HTTP router: chi v5 (net/http compatible)
- DB driver/pool: pgx/v5 + pgxpool (PostGIS, ST_DWithin, pg_trgm)
- Query building: Masterminds/squirrel
- AuthN: golang-jwt/jwt v5 (HS256, aud via ClaimStrings) + X-API-Key (constant-time compare)
- Validation: go-playground/validator v10
- Config: spf13/viper (flat env scheme: DATABASE_URL, AUTH_JWT_SECRET, SERVER_PORT, ... no prefix)
- In-process cache: dgraph-io/ristretto v2
- Observability: go.opentelemetry.io/otel + otlphttp exporter + otelhttp middleware; structured logging via log/slog
- API docs: swaggo/swag (Swagger UI at /docs)
- Tests/mocks: testify + hand-written mocks
- Migrations: golang-migrate file format (skip_migrations defaults true; gold schema externally managed)
- Container: multi-stage Dockerfile -> distroless runtime; docker-compose with postgis/postgis:17-3.5

== CONSTRAINTS / CONTEXT ==
- Deployment target: ON-PREMISE (no AWS/GCP managed services). BGN = Indonesian government nutrition agency.
- Compliance/sensitivity: handles beneficiary PII; Indonesian gov context (SPBE, UU PDP). Security-sensitive.
- Gateway: Kong already in front (owns /v1 versioning, likely TLS termination, possibly rate limiting / auth).
- Read-heavy, latency-sensitive reads over a gold OLAP schema. Geospatial (PostGIS) + fuzzy search (pg_trgm).

== KNOWN GAPS / OPEN ITEMS (address these in the recommendation) ==
1. CI/CD: no pipeline yet (Makefile targets exist). On-prem — likely GitLab CI (repo host is sipgn-git.bgn.go.id) or Jenkins. Recommend a concrete on-prem CI approach + quality gates (build, test, lint, vuln scan, container scan).
2. Secrets management: a .env with plaintext DB creds was found (being rotated). Recommend an on-prem secrets approach (Vault? sealed secrets? env injection) — no cloud secrets manager available.
3. Linting/static analysis: no golangci-lint/staticcheck config committed. Recommend a Go linting + security-scan stack (golangci-lint, gosec, govulncheck).
4. Observability BACKEND not chosen (only OTLP exporter exists). Recommend an on-prem-friendly stack (Tempo/Jaeger for traces, Prometheus + Grafana for metrics, Loki for logs) and whether to add Prometheus metrics to the Go service.
5. Rate limiting: an unused RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED error variant exists; service has none. Decide: rely on Kong, or add in-service limiting (and which lib).
6. Runtime/orchestration on-prem: bare Docker? docker-compose? Kubernetes (on-prem, e.g. k3s/RKE)? Nomad? Recommend given a single read-mostly service + BGN scale.
7. Migrations runner: make migrate is a placeholder; gold schema externally managed. Recommend how migrations should actually be run/owned given read-only gold.
8. Dockerfile go-version skew: builder is golang:1.22 but module is go 1.25 (docker build would fail) — note as a fix.
9. Load/perf testing + caching strategy: ristretto in-process only; consider whether a shared cache (Redis on-prem) is warranted for read scaling behind Kong.

Produce: (A) a verdict on the CURRENT stack (keep/strong fits + any risky choices), (B) a Tech Radar style recommendation (Adopt/Trial/Hold) for the GAP areas above tailored to on-prem + gov + read-mostly, with concrete library/tool picks and 1-line rationale each, (C) a short prioritized action list (what to add first). Keep it practical and specific to this service; avoid generic filler.
